rows.capability: Whole-package torch_ecg runtime dependency
rows.reason: The donor would add a broad PyTorch/scientific/data-download dependency graph that is unnecessary for the governed target. No whole-package runtime dependency is approved.

rows.capability: Config-driven preprocessing manager and registry
rows.reason: Target requires explicit provenance-bound transformations. Donor manager can randomize order and silently ignores unknown config items; do not use it as canonical preprocessing authority.

rows.capability: Bandpass, baseline removal, normalization and resampling preprocessors
rows.reason: WFDB and NeuroKit donors already cover these transformation families. Target keeps native calibrated source evidence and does not need another canonical preprocessing implementation.

rows.capability: Baseline-wander and noise robustness augmentation
rows.reason: Useful robustness-fixture ideas, but synthetic distortions are engineering evidence only and OpenECG/NeuroKit already provide comparable augmentation concepts.

rows.capability: CutMix, MixUp, masking, renormalization and stretch/compress augmentation
rows.reason: Potential offline challenger-training robustness techniques only. They must not modify governed source evidence or imply diagnostic validity.

rows.capability: Label smoothing augmentation
rows.reason: Training-only regularization with no current governed target need and no runtime role.

rows.capability: Local ECG database reader and dataset adapter abstractions
rows.reason: Broad format/dataset access is useful future adapter knowledge, but each database has separate source, licensing and provenance requirements and no current target source requirement justifies adoption.

rows.capability: Remote PhysioNet/HTTP/S3/Google Drive data acquisition
rows.reason: Mutable remote resolution, network credentials/provider semantics and automatic download/extraction conflict with the target exact-source and substitution controls for governed execution.

rows.capability: Bundled physiological sample-data and annotations
rows.reason: 266 sample-data files are tracked, but no dataset-specific LICENSE/COPYING/TERMS file was found under sample-data. Software MIT terms are not treated as data-use or redistribution rights. No bytes are imported.

rows.capability: ECG CRNN/FCN classification architecture family
rows.reason: Architecture family may support future isolated model challengers, but no tracked checkpoint exists and upstream architecture provenance includes other repositories. No execution or authority is granted.

rows.capability: ECG sequence-labeling architecture family
rows.reason: Sequence labeling could challenge event localization, but no exact licensed checkpoint is present and the implementation has CPSC2019 lineage. Retain only as future challenger architecture knowledge.

rows.capability: ECG U-Net and subtract-U-Net wave delineation architectures
rows.reason: Potential future delineation challengers only. No exact checkpoint identity, weight license or target validation is available.

rows.capability: RR-LSTM interval-model architecture
rows.reason: Could support future interval-based challenger research, but no checkpoint or validation evidence is admitted and no runtime authority is added.

rows.capability: Generic CNN backbone library including ResNet, MultiScopicNet, DenseNet and Xception
rows.reason: Large architecture catalog has mixed upstream provenance and no exact donor checkpoint identity. Audit original upstreams before any model-specific reuse.

rows.capability: Transformer architecture utilities
rows.reason: Generic model-building capability with no current target need, exact checkpoint or ECG-specific governed evidence.

rows.capability: Model/backbone/attention registries and model configuration catalog
rows.reason: Useful design pattern for experimentation, but target already uses explicit machine-readable challenger registries and should not introduce dynamic Python model registration into governed runtime.

rows.capability: Task output containers for classification, sequence tagging, delineation and R-peaks
rows.reason: Target challenger envelopes already provide stricter provenance hashes, input identity, valid-window guards, abstention and explicit non-authority fields. Donor containers allow arbitrary custom fields and are weaker for governed evidence.

rows.capability: Classification metric suite
rows.reason: Metric implementations may inform offline evaluation, but zero adjudicated project gold means target diagnostic metrics remain NOT_REPORTABLE and donor labels/results cannot establish clinical performance.

rows.capability: R-peak challenge scoring with temporal tolerance
rows.reason: Tolerance-based event scoring is useful evaluation methodology but overlaps prior WFDB/NeuroKit event comparison work and cannot become a reportable clinical metric without governed gold.

rows.capability: Wave delineation sensitivity/precision/F1 and timing-error metrics
rows.reason: Useful offline delineation evaluation, overlapping OpenECG boundary metrics. Donor benchmark labels are source labels only and target metrics remain NOT_REPORTABLE.

rows.capability: Generic training loop, logging, model selection and checkpoint management
rows.reason: Training infrastructure is not part of the governed ECG runtime. Model selection on donor/benchmark metrics cannot transfer clinical authority.

rows.capability: Safetensors-first checkpoint serialization and safe-load pattern
rows.reason: The safer serialization/loading pattern is useful for future isolated challenger execution, but the current JavaScript target does not load PyTorch checkpoints. Preserve as a security requirement, not a runtime dependency.

rows.capability: Pickle-compatible torch.load fallback including weights_only=False
rows.reason: Untrusted pickle-capable checkpoint deserialization is incompatible with fail-closed governed execution. Any future loader must require exact artifact identity and a non-executable safe format or equivalent isolated controls.

rows.capability: Remote model download and immediate checkpoint loading
rows.reason: Mutable remote model retrieval without a target-owned exact hash/license/provenance admission gate violates source-substitution controls.

rows.capability: WFDB XQRS/GQRS detector wrappers
rows.reason: Canonical upstream was already audited under DONOR-001. Do not reattribute or duplicate those algorithms through torch_ecg.

rows.capability: BioSPPy-derived traditional R-peak detector wrappers
rows.reason: The donor documents BioSPPy lineage. Any future reuse must audit the original upstream rather than treating torch_ecg as canonical algorithm provenance.

rows.capability: ECG plotting implementation modified from ecg-image-kit
rows.reason: Canonical upstream is the already-scheduled DONOR-005 alphanumericslab/ecg-image-kit. Defer image-rendering assessment to that donor.

rows.capability: WFDB header/data utilities modified from wfdb-python
rows.reason: Canonical upstream was audited as DONOR-001; target already has a bounded native WFDB substrate.

rows.capability: Challenge benchmark training pipelines and task datasets
rows.reason: Pipelines are valuable research references but several are migrated from separate repositories and the donor warns some are outdated or incompletely tested. They are not target runtime or gold evidence.

rows.capability: Bundled benchmark logs, result CSVs and reported scores
rows.reason: Historical donor results are not reproduced target evidence, are not comparable across datasets as clinical truth and cannot be promoted to project metrics.

rows.capability: Python CI/test matrix, coverage and model/database test workflows
rows.reason: Useful QA patterns, but upstream tests include external database/download behavior and are not hermetic. Target retains its own exact-source CI and may selectively adopt test ideas only.

rows.capability: Incomplete or explicitly excluded SSL, NAS, Grad-CAM and model surfaces
rows.reason: Upstream coverage configuration marks these as incomplete or omitted. Do not promote unfinished donor surfaces.

rows.capability: Checkpoint metadata conventions for model/train configuration
rows.reason: Explicit model/train config metadata alongside weights is a useful future provenance requirement, but it does not establish checkpoint identity, licensing, training population or clinical validity by itself.

rows.capability: Clinical/source provenance, authority separation and fail-closed governance
rows.reason: torch_ecg is a research framework, not the target governed authority system. Existing target governance is stronger and must not be weakened.

cross_donor_deduplication.wfdb_lineage: XQRS/GQRS and WFDB-derived utilities are superseded by canonical DONOR-001 review.
cross_donor_deduplication.neurokit_overlap: Preprocessing, detector diversity, event agreement and synthetic robustness concepts overlap DONOR-003; do not add another canonical implementation.
cross_donor_deduplication.openecg_overlap: Boundary metrics, challenger output representation and robustness augmentation concepts overlap DONOR-002.
cross_donor_deduplication.ecg_image_kit: torch_ecg plotting code identifies alphanumericslab/ecg-image-kit lineage; canonical assessment is deferred to scheduled DONOR-005.
cross_donor_deduplication.biosppy_and_architecture_upstreams: BioSPPy and architecture-source repositories are provenance references only in this donor. Audit original upstream separately before any future source reuse.
